DIRECTOR OF FOOTBALL — built and shipped.

These artboards are the design; the app now matches them. See src/ui/colour.ts for the club-colour rule and src/ui/advance.ts for the button.

The direction.

Terminal's density and typography, Floodlight's pill and icon nav, a club-coloured header, and one contextual advance button.

Row below: the three directions this came out of, kept for reference.

HOME — a dashboard with hierarchy, not a tile grid

A uniform grid of boxes is the thing that made the old build feel busy, and copying FC Pro's version just reproduced it in darker paint. So nothing here is the same size or shape as anything else:

· The standing is 66px and unchallenged — it is why you opened the app. Board confidence sits directly under it with a target marker, because position-against-target is what drives it.
· The next match gets its own raised band and the opponent's colour. It is the one scheduled event, so it looks like an event.
· Decisions read as an inbox: severity bar, headline, mono detail line.
· The six departments are one small bar chart, not six tiles. Same information, a quarter of the space, and a weak department is visible without knowing the scale. Each bar is its own tap target.

Everything is still tappable. It just no longer looks like a menu.

SQUAD — the density test

Same header, back chevron and filter in the club band. The status strip carries the constraints you would otherwise go hunting for: registered 24/25, non-homegrown 16/17, wage ratio.

13 rows without scrolling versus 8 in the card layouts, and nothing is boxed. Rating is the only coloured column; KNK / BID / HG are the only other ink.

THE ADVANCE BUTTON

"Advance to Week 23" is the wrong label — a week number is an engine detail, and nobody wants week 23. A bare "Advance" is also wrong: it hides what you are about to set off, and some weeks are dangerous to step through.

So: one button, one place, two lines. A verb phrase naming the next real event, and a mono line carrying the week's actual contents.

It blocks only on things that expire if ignored — an offer about to lapse, a contract entering its last six weeks. You can still refuse them; you just cannot sleepwalk past them. It never blocks to make you read something.

CLUB COLOUR — readable, always

Painting a header the raw club colour breaks on yellow, white and near-black. The rule: primary to HSL, lightness clamped into 10-17%, chroma capped, plus an untouched 3px strip beneath so the real colour stays on screen.

White primaries fall through to the secondary. Near-blacks lift instead of clamping. Six worst cases shown; every one clears 4.5:1 with white text.

Nothing below the strip is club-coloured.
EARLIER DIRECTIONS — kept for reference, not proposed.
